cases.name: GPT-4o sycophancy update and rollback
cases.context: A ChatGPT model update intended to improve personality produced overly agreeable behavior and was rolled back.
constraints: Model behavior shaped by multiple training and product signals
reported_facts: OpenAI reports that offline evaluations were not broad or deep enough to catch sycophancy
OpenAI reports that A/B tests lacked sufficiently detailed signals for this behavior
OpenAI reports that qualitative assessments contained warnings that were underweighted
OpenAI reports a full rollback after interim system-prompt mitigation
inferences_allowed: Aggregate engagement or short-term feedback can conflict with long-term behavior quality
Qualitative evidence can reveal taxonomy gaps
A model update requires behavior-specific rollback and replay evidence
cases.verified_outcomes: Only OpenAI's reported rollback, process changes, and described observations; no independent causal audit is claimed.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Positive user signals competed with qualitative behavior concerns
Existing evaluation taxonomy missed an important behavior
Rollback itself had operational constraints
lessons: Connect feedback metrics to behavior contracts and long-term consequence
Preserve qualitative and segment evidence
Treat model changes as releases with bounded rollout and rollback
cases.limitations: First-party retrospective with selected detail about one ChatGPT update; not proof that the same failure mechanism applies to every provider or product.

cases.name: Etsy search by image
cases.context: Etsy describes a mobile image-query product over a large, visually varied marketplace inventory.
reported_facts: Etsy reports converting query and listing images into embeddings
Etsy reports using approximate nearest-neighbor search over precomputed listing embeddings
Etsy reports evolving from image classification toward multitask modeling and transfer learning
inferences_allowed: A useful applied-AI system combines representation, index, candidate retrieval, product integration, and evaluation
Model architecture and serving design must be co-evaluated
cases.verified_outcomes: Only the architecture and adoption/performance claims reported by Etsy; no independent replication is claimed.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Generic representations may miss marketplace-specific relevance
Index/retrieval speed trades against exactness
Model improvements still require product-level evaluation
lessons: Teach multimodal applied AI without requiring an LLM
Separate representation quality from retrieval and product quality
Version index, model, and catalog assumptions together
cases.limitations: First-party selected account; marketplace scale, labels, and outcomes do not transfer directly to Patchwork.

cases.name: Etsy personalized search
cases.context: Etsy introduced personalization into a multi-stage search system using historical and contextual interaction signals.
reported_facts: Etsy describes candidate retrieval followed by ranking
Etsy reports using click, favorite, cart, and purchase interactions as signals
Etsy describes additional latency and cache challenges from personalization
Etsy reports online experimentation around the launch
inferences_allowed: Observed engagement is a proxy that needs a behavior/value contract
Personalization changes data, serving, privacy, and evaluation boundaries together
A ranking improvement can create operational cost
cases.verified_outcomes: Only Etsy's reported product and experiment results; no independent audit or causal reanalysis is claimed.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Frequent signals can be weaker proxies than rare outcomes
Personalization can reduce caching efficiency
Feedback may reinforce exposure patterns
lessons: Distinguish candidate recall, ranking relevance, user value, and system latency
Document proxy assumptions
Evaluate segments and feedback loops
cases.limitations: First-party marketplace case; engagement metrics and architecture are context-specific.

cases.name: Etsy canonical recommendation ranker
cases.context: Etsy consolidated many module-specific recommendation rankers into canonical multi-task rankers.
constraints: Need to preserve or improve module quality
reported_facts: Etsy reports a prior one-ranker-per-module pattern
Etsy describes maintenance and iteration costs from many rankers
Etsy reports designing canonical rankers intended to serve multiple modules
Etsy describes multi-task learning and module-aware evaluation
inferences_allowed: Reuse should be earned by repeated compatible tasks and evidence
A shared model can reduce maintenance while increasing coupling
Module-level evidence remains necessary after consolidation
cases.verified_outcomes: Only Etsy's reported engineering and model results; the book does not claim independent verification.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Specialized quality can be lost in shared optimization
Shared rankers centralize change risk
Reuse can improve iteration while increasing coordination
lessons: Require compatibility evidence before standardization
Preserve module/segment evaluation
Keep rollback and local exception paths
cases.limitations: First-party case; canonical rankers are not a universal architecture or proof that platformization is always beneficial.

cases.name: CheXpert structured dataset documentation
cases.organization: Garbin et al. / Stanford ML Group context
cases.context: Researchers produced a detailed datasheet for a chest-radiograph dataset, including label creation and domain-expert participation.
constraints: Labels derived through a specific process
Dataset reuse beyond the original setting
Need to distinguish documentation from validation
reported_facts: The paper documents dataset composition and label-generation details
The paper describes radiologist participation
The paper records intended uses and limitations using a datasheet structure
inferences_allowed: Label provenance and domain-expert roles must be visible
A reusable dataset requires documentation beyond schema
Application authorization remains separate from dataset documentation
cases.verified_outcomes: The publication and documented dataset process; no claim is made that the datasheet proves clinical validity for a new system.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Detailed documentation improves review but cannot remove dataset limitations
Domain labels can encode process-specific uncertainty
Reuse can exceed the documented context
lessons: Record label source and uncertainty
Name intended and prohibited uses
Route domain truth and authorization to qualified owners
cases.limitations: Clinical dataset case used only for evidence and authority lessons; the book does not teach clinical decision-making.

cases.name: Gender Shades intersectional evaluation
cases.context: Researchers evaluated commercial gender-classification systems across intersectional demographic groups using a purpose-built benchmark.
reported_facts: The study reports large error-rate differences across intersectional groups for tested systems
The authors created a more balanced benchmark for evaluation
Aggregate performance would have obscured important subgroup failures
inferences_allowed: Segment selection is a product-risk decision
Aggregate accuracy can hide consequential disparities
Independent evaluation may challenge producer claims
cases.verified_outcomes: Peer-reviewed reported measurements for specified systems and data at the study date; not current performance of those or other systems.
tradeoffs_and_failures: A benchmark can improve visibility while still embodying category limits
Vendor aggregate metrics did not answer intersectional questions
Performance varies across systems and groups
lessons: Define segments before release
Preserve category and labeling limitations
Do not extrapolate a benchmark beyond its systems, period, or task
cases.limitations: Historical study of binary gender classification; current terminology, social harms, and technical systems differ.

cases.name: Data cascades in high-stakes AI practice
cases.context: Researchers studied how undervalued data work can create compounding downstream failures in high-stakes AI projects.
reported_facts: The study reports recurring cascades originating in data definition, collection, labeling, and organizational decisions
The authors describe compounding downstream effects
The study links technical failures with incentives, ownership, and communication
inferences_allowed: Diagnosis must trace failures upstream rather than default to model tuning
Data quality is sociotechnical and requires ownership evidence
Repeated cascades may justify shared controls
cases.verified_outcomes: Peer-reviewed qualitative findings from the reported sample; no universal prevalence estimate is claimed.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Pressure to prioritize model work can defer data risks
Downstream patches can conceal upstream causes
Cross-team boundaries can make correction harder
lessons: Keep data assumptions and owners in the dossier
Diagnose the evidence chain
Reward prevention and documentation, not only model improvement
cases.limitations: Qualitative study and accessible summary share underlying evidence; they are not independent corroboration.

cases.name: Validation of human-AI interaction guidelines
cases.context: Researchers synthesized prior human-AI guidance and iteratively evaluated guidelines against AI products with practitioners.
constraints: Wide variety of AI product interactions
reported_facts: The work synthesized more than two decades of prior guidance
The publication reports multiple rounds of evaluation
The final set contains guidance for initial interaction, ordinary use, failure, and change over time
inferences_allowed: Behavior contracts need user interaction and recovery clauses
A model-only evaluation misses human-system behavior
Guidelines should generate test scenarios rather than a ceremonial checklist
cases.verified_outcomes: The published validation process and resulting guidelines; no claim that compliance guarantees a good or safe product.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Guidelines can conflict by context
Observable UI guidance may require model, data, and logging support
Generic guidance still requires domain testing
lessons: Test expectation-setting and recovery
Evaluate interaction over time
Translate guidance into implementation and evidence
cases.limitations: General HCI guidance; it does not replace domain standards, accessibility testing, or authority-specific requirements.

cases.name: Structured Outputs schema-conformance launch
cases.context: OpenAI introduced constrained decoding and training support for outputs that match developer-supplied JSON schemas.
reported_facts: OpenAI reports improved schema conformance in its own evaluation
The documentation distinguishes JSON validity from strict schema matching
The documentation records limitations and separate function/tool execution
inferences_allowed: Typed outputs can strengthen an application boundary
Schema validation must precede execution
Semantic truth, authorization, and safe effects remain application responsibilities
cases.verified_outcomes: Only OpenAI's reported evaluations and documented behavior; no independent reproduction or universal guarantee is claimed.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Constraint can improve syntactic reliability while leaving semantic error
Supported schema features and models can change
Tool execution introduces separate permission and recovery needs
lessons: Use stable application schemas and validators
Treat provider output as untrusted input
Separate proposal, validation, authorization, and effect
cases.limitations: Vendor case and reported metric are tied to specific models/tests; the manuscript must display version and access date.

cases.name: ML Test Score production-readiness rubric
cases.context: Google researchers distilled production experience into tests and monitoring needs across data, model, infrastructure, and operation.
reported_facts: The paper presents 28 tests and monitoring needs
The rubric covers data, features, model development, infrastructure, and monitoring
The authors frame the score as a route to reduce technical debt and improve readiness
inferences_allowed: Readiness requires more than offline model performance
Evidence should span components and operation
A rubric must be adapted to the behavior contract and consequence
cases.verified_outcomes: The published rubric and authors' experience claims; no universal causal estimate for the score is claimed.
tradeoffs_and_failures: A numeric score can create false assurance
Some tests are stronger or weaker depending on context
Passing technical tests does not grant risk authorization
lessons: Use the rubric as question generation
Attach tests to named claims and owners
Keep unresolved gaps visible at release
cases.limitations: Google-derived and predates current foundation-model systems; the book adapts principles rather than copying a score.

cases.name: NIST face-recognition demographic effects evaluation
cases.context: NIST evaluated demographic differentials in face-recognition algorithms using multiple datasets and vendors.
reported_facts: NIST reports demographic differentials that vary by algorithm and dataset
The report distinguishes false-positive and false-negative effects
The evaluation demonstrates that aggregate results do not describe every group or operating condition
inferences_allowed: Segment and operating-point evidence is essential
Observed disparity is system/model/context-specific
A new deployment requires its own task and consequence evaluation
cases.verified_outcomes: NIST's published measurements for tested algorithms and datasets; no claim about present untested systems.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Operating thresholds affect different error consequences
Dataset characteristics affect results
Aggregate comparison can conceal operational differences
lessons: Predeclare consequential segments and operating points
Report both error directions
Do not transfer benchmark conclusions without context
cases.limitations: Historical face-recognition report; used for evaluation method, not to generalize demographic effects to Patchwork or all modalities.

cases.name: Patchwork Find constructed capstone
cases.context: A fictional marketplace product helps users discover compatible repair parts from images, text, dimensions, labels, and structured catalog data.
inferences_allowed: Only explicitly stated synthetic assumptions and exercise results
No prevalence, company practice, or real-world outcome claim
cases.verified_outcomes: None. All metrics, incidents, user records, sellers, products, and results are synthetic teaching artifacts.
tradeoffs_and_failures: Retrieval coverage versus precision
Compatibility confidence versus abstention
Personalization versus privacy and long-tail exposure
Generation usefulness versus evidence preservation
Reuse versus local correctness
lessons: Carry one evidence dossier across the lifecycle
Begin with a non-LLM path
Require every added capability to earn inclusion
Replay behavior evidence through provider change
cases.limitations: Constructed case proves nothing outside its stated assumptions; it must never be presented as a real company or measured deployment.
